topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: The Problem: Average vs. Instantaneous Speed
lecture_lines: Average speed is total distance over total time. [Asset: cheetah_run]
But what is speed at one specific moment? [Asset: speedometer_needle]
Calculus helps us find this instantaneous speed. [Asset: flash_freeze]

sections.title: Visualizing the Limit: From Secant to Tangent
lecture_lines: We plot position versus time on a graph. [Asset: curve_plot]
A secant line connects two distinct points. [Asset: secant_line]
Shrinking the interval makes the secant move. [Asset: shrinking_interval]
As interval nears zero, it becomes tangent. [Asset: tangent_line]
This limit gives us the instantaneous rate. [Asset: limit_arrow]

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
lecture_lines: The derivative is the slope of the tangent. [Asset: tangent_slope_highlight]
Formula: limit as h approaches zero of slope. [Asset: derivative_formula]
This measures change at an exact point. [Asset: point_magnification]
Secant slope represents average change over h. [Asset: secant_slope_h]
The limit reveals the instantaneous rate. [Asset: slope_convergence]

sections.title: Application: The Falling Drone
lecture_lines: Imagine a drone dropping a package. [Asset: drone_hover]
Height changes according to gravity over time. [Asset: height_curve]
The derivative function tells us exact velocity. [Asset: velocity_graph]

sections.title: Summary and Intuition Check
lecture_lines: The derivative is the tangent line's slope. [Asset: slope_tangent_summary]
It represents the instantaneous rate of change. [Asset: rate_change_text]
Slopes reveal peaks, valleys, and trends. [Asset: mountain_slopes]
